questions.question: The parliamentary standing committees have a tenure of _____ year(s).
questions.solution: Parliamentary Standing Committees are permanent committees constituted periodically (usually every year) and have a tenure of one year. This is in contrast to Ad Hoc committees which exist only for a specific task.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding State Legislatures?
A. Notwithstanding anything in part XVII, but subject to the provisions of Article 348, business in the Legislature of a State shall be transacted in the official language or languages of the State or in Hindi or in English.
B. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or Chairman of the Legislative Council can permit any member to speak in his mother tongue.
C. Only the Supreme Court is entitled to inquire into the proceedings of the State Legislature.
questions.solution: Statements A and B are correct regarding the language used in State Legislatures. Statement C is incorrect because Article 212 states that the validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a State shall not be called in question in any court (including the Supreme Court) on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished in 2019 through the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act.
2. The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished in 2020 through the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct. The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 led to the abolition of the state's Upper House (Legislative Council) and the bifurcation of the state into Union Territories in 2019.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Meghalaya has two Lok Sabha seats, namely Shillong and Tura.
2. Meghalaya has one Rajya Sabha seat.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Meghalaya is represented by two members in the Lok Sabha (from Shillong and Tura constituencies) and one member in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha after India’s Independence?
questions.solution: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha (1952–1956) and is often referred to as the 'Father of Lok Sabha'. M.A. Ayyangar was the first Deputy Speaker.

questions.question: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of how many years?
questions.solution: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and does not dissolve. However, its members are elected for a fixed term of 6 years, with one-third of the members retiring every two years.

questions.question: Who elects the Presiding Officer (the speaker) in the State legislature?
questions.solution: The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is elected by the members of the Vidhan Sabha from among themselves, as per Article 178.

questions.question: The First hour of a sitting of the House allotted for asking and answering of questions is called as __________.
questions.solution: The Question Hour is the first hour of every parliamentary sitting where members ask questions to ministers to hold the executive accountable. Zero Hour typically follows immediately after the Question Hour.

questions.question: A money bill under Article 111 of the Constitution of India, presented to the President for assent, has to be endorsed by a Certificate of the ________signed by him/her that it is a money bill.
questions.option_1: Secretary General of the Lok Sabha
questions.option_2: Secretary General of the Rajya Sabha
questions.option_4: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.solution: Under Article 110(4), when a Money Bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha or presented to the President, it must carry a certificate from the Speaker of the Lok Sabha confirming that it is indeed a Money Bill. The Speaker's decision on this is final.

questions.question: After how many days of absence from Parliament without permission will a Member of Parliament be disqualified?
questions.solution: According to Article 101(4), if a member of either House of Parliament is absent for a period of 60 days without the permission of the House, their seat may be declared vacant.

questions.question: What is the bicameral legislature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: It is a legislative body with four houses.
questions.option_2: It is a legislative body with two houses.
questions.option_3: It is a legislative body with one house.
questions.option_4: It is a legislative body with three houses.
questions.solution: A bicameral legislature means a system with two houses. In India, at the Union level, these are the Lok Sabha (Lower House) and the Rajya Sabha (Upper House).

questions.question: What is the most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability?
questions.solution: The No-confidence motion is the most powerful tool. If passed in the Lok Sabha, the entire Council of Ministers must resign, demonstrating that the executive is collectively responsible to the legislature.

questions.question: What is the maximum time gap between two sessions of the State Legislature?
questions.solution: Under Article 174, the gap between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session must not exceed six months. This ensures the legislature meets at least twice a year.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched regarding the terminology used in the Parliament?
A. Appropriation Bill - A Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India
B. Demand for Grants - Earmarking of budgetary allocation for meeting only planned expenditure of a Ministry/Department
C. Short Duration Discussion - For raising a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance for which a notice has to be given by a Member and supported by 50 Members.
questions.solution: Only Pair A is correctly matched. Demand for Grants (B) includes both planned and non-planned estimated expenditure. Short Duration Discussion (C) does not require the support of 50 members; that requirement is specifically for an Adjournment Motion or a No-Confidence Motion.

questions.question: Which of the following can make provisions for Ancillary powers of the Supreme Court?
questions.solution: Under Article 140, the Parliament may by law confer upon the Supreme Court such supplemental powers as may appear to be necessary to enable the Court to exercise its jurisdiction effectively.

questions.question: In India, during a meeting of the Legislative Assembly or Council, if there is no quorum, it shall be the duty of the ________ to adjourn the House or suspend the meeting.
questions.solution: According to Article 189(3), the Speaker (in the Assembly) or the Chairman (in the Council) is responsible for adjourning or suspending the House if the required quorum (1/10th of total members) is not present.

questions.question: A Money Bill should be returned to the Lok Sabha within ___ days by Rajya Sabha, either with recommendations or without recommendations.
questions.solution: The Rajya Sabha has limited powers regarding Money Bills. It must return the bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days. If it fails to do so, the bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form it was passed by the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Archana wishes to contest for Lok Sabha elections in India. What is the maximum limit of constituencies that she can contest?
questions.solution: Under Section 33(7) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate is allowed to contest from a maximum of two constituencies in a general election or a group of bye-elections.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a kind of question related to Indian Parliamentary Proceedings?
questions.solution: Valid question types include Starred (oral answer), Unstarred (written answer), and Short Notice (urgent matters). There is no such category as a 'Long Notice Question'.

questions.question: Which of the following is called 'the temple of the country's democracy'?
questions.solution: The Parliament of India is often metaphorically referred to as the 'temple of democracy' as it is the supreme legislative body where the representatives of the people meet to frame laws and debate national issues.

questions.question: The state legislative assembly has a strength of ____, with exceptions for smaller states.
questions.solution: As per the Constitution, a State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) should have between 60 and 500 members. However, exceptions exist for smaller states like Goa, Sikkim, and Mizoram where the number is less than 60.

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, the House of People shall consist of not more than ______ members to represent the Union territories.
questions.solution: Article 81 specifies that the Lok Sabha shall have a maximum of 530 members from States and not more than twenty members to represent the Union Territories.

questions.question: How many organs of government are there according to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: There are three organs: The Legislature (makes laws), The Executive (enforces laws), and The Judiciary (interprets laws).

questions.question: __________ is a motion moved by a member to cut short the debate on a matter before the House.
questions.solution: A Closure Motion is a procedure by which a member can request that the debate on a particular matter be closed immediately so that the matter can be put to a vote.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of parliamentary government in India?
questions.option_1: Membership of the ministers in the legislature,
questions.option_3: Presence of nominal and real executives
questions.option_4: Collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature
questions.solution: In a parliamentary system, the Lower House (Lok Sabha) IS dissolvable by the President. The Upper House (Rajya Sabha) is the one that is permanent and undissolvable.
